base_cards.front: Translate: actuellement.
back: Currently.

base_cards.front: Translate: une librairie.
back: A bookshop.

base_cards.front: Translate: ne...que.
back: Only.

base_cards.front: Translate: malgré.
back: Despite.

base_cards.front: Translate: sauf.
back: Except.

base_cards.front: Translate: trop cher.
back: Too expensive.

base_cards.front: Translate: rapidement.
back: Quickly.

base_cards.front: Translate: la semaine dernière.
back: Last week.

base_cards.front: Translate: à l'avenir.
back: In future.

base_cards.front: Translate: je voudrais.
back: I would like.

base_cards.front: Read: Ma sœur adore la musique, mais mon frère préfère lire. Give each person's preference.
back: Sister: music.
Brother: reading.

base_cards.front: Read: Avant, je détestais le sport. Maintenant, je joue au tennis tous les jours. Give the earlier opinion and present activity.
back: Used to hate sport.
Now plays tennis every day.

base_cards.front: Read: Le village est calme, mais il manque des magasins. Give an advantage and a disadvantage.
back: It is quiet.
There is a lack of shops.

base_cards.front: Read: Les billets ne sont pas chers, mais le voyage est long. Give the positive and negative.
back: Tickets are not expensive.
The journey is long.

base_cards.front: Translate: Je viens de finir mes devoirs.
back: I have just finished my homework.

base_cards.front: Translate: J'habite ici depuis deux ans.
back: I have lived here for two years.
The action still continues.

base_cards.front: Translate: Je ne regarde plus la télévision.
back: I no longer watch television.

base_cards.front: Explain what les refers to in Les livres sont chers, mais je les achète.
back: The books. Les is a direct object pronoun replacing les livres.

base_cards.front: Infer the meaning of impossible in Cette solution est impossible, and identify the word-family clue.
back: Impossible; im- gives the opposite of possible.

base_cards.front: Infer consommateur from consommer and a shopping context.
back: A consumer. The agent ending refers to a person who consumes/buys products.

base_cards.front: Translate: Hier, nous avons pris le bus parce que les billets étaient moins chers.
back: Yesterday, we took the bus because the tickets were cheaper.
Keep the past event, reason and comparison.

base_cards.front: Translate: Je voudrais travailler dans une librairie, mais ma sœur préfère la bibliothèque.
back: I would like to work in a bookshop, but my sister prefers the library.
Do not confuse librairie and bibliothèque.

base_cards.front: Translate: Il n'y a pas assez de bus, donc je vais à pied au collège.
back: There are not enough buses, so I walk to school.
Not enough does not mean no buses.

base_cards.front: Translate: Les amis que je retrouve au parc sont très gentils.
back: The friends whom/that I meet in the park are very kind.
Que introduces the people met; très modifies kind.

base_cards.front: Translate: L'année dernière, j'ai passé une semaine en France. La ville était belle, mais il pleuvait souvent. À l'avenir, je vais voyager en train.
back: Last year, I spent a week in France. The town/city was beautiful, but it often rained / was often raining. In future, I am going to travel by train.
Preserve the completed visit, background weather, frequency and future plan.

base_cards.front: Explain four checks to make after translating a passage into English.
back: Every phrase is included.
Subjects and pronoun references are correct.
Time frames and negatives are preserved.
Numbers, comparisons and qualifiers retain their precise meanings.

additions.front: Translate: Elle ne travaille plus ici.
back: She no longer works here.

additions.front: Translate: Il n’a que deux euros.
back: He only has two euros.

additions.front: Translate: Nous n’avons pas encore fini.
back: We have not finished yet.
I must leave.

additions.front: Translate: Mes amis veulent visiter le musée.
back: My friends want to visit the museum.

additions.front: Translate: Je préfère rester chez moi.
back: I prefer to stay at home.
I have too much homework.

additions.front: Why must you track a subject change after mais?
back: The next opinion or action may belong to a different person. Otherwise you may attribute the wrong preference.

additions.front: May natural English use a different word order from French?
back: Yes, provided it preserves the complete meaning, including time, negatives, comparisons and who does what.

additions.front: What is lost by translating “ne travaille plus” as simply “does not work”?
back: The meaning no longer: it signals that the earlier situation has changed.
Identify exactly which earlier person or thing a pronoun replaces, then keep that reference clear in the answer.

additions.front: What should be checked after writing a natural English version?
back: Compare it phrase by phrase with the French to find omitted or changed meaning.

additions.front: Why should a cognate be checked in context?
back: A familiar-looking word may be a false friend or may have a different meaning in that particular sentence.
She answers quickly.
